title.zh: 卷七十五 志第二十六: 祭祀四
title.raw: 卷七十五 志第二十六: 祭祀四 Volume 75 Treatises 28: Offerings 4

sentences.zh: 祭祀四 ○宗廟下親謝儀，其目有八：

translations.literal: Offerings 4. Under the Ancestral Temple section: the ceremony in which the emperor personally offers thanks—its categories number eight:
translations.idiomatic: Offerings 4: Ancestral Temple—the imperial thanksgiving rite. The procedure comprises eight stages:

sentences.zh: 一曰齋戒。

translations.literal: The first is purification and abstention.
translations.idiomatic: The first stage is ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 前享三日，皇帝散齋二日於別殿，致齋一日於大次。

translations.literal: Three days before the offering, the emperor observes preliminary abstention for two days in a separate hall and strict abstention for one day in the grand tent.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the sacrifice, the emperor spends two days in preliminary fasting in a side hall and one day in strict fasting in the grand pavilion.

sentences.zh: 應享官員受誓戒於中書省，如常儀。

translations.literal: Officials attending the offering receive the abstention oath at the Central Secretariat, according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: All officials who are to take part receive the purification oath at the Central Secretariat, in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 二曰陳設，如前親祀儀。

translations.literal: The second is arranging the offerings, as in the earlier ceremony for personal imperial sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The second stage is the arrangement of ritual furnishings, as prescribed in the personal imperial sacrifice ceremony described above.

sentences.zh: 三曰車駕出宮。

translations.literal: The third is the imperial procession leaving the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The third stage is the emperor's departure from the palace.

sentences.zh: 前享一日，所司備儀從、內外仗，與應享之官兩行序立於崇天門外，太僕卿控御馬立於大明門外，諸侍臣及導駕官二十四人，俱於齋殿前左右分班立俟。

translations.literal: One day before the offering, the responsible offices prepare the retinue and inner and outer guards; officials attending the offering stand in two ranks outside the Chongtian Gate; the Minister of Imperial Studs holds the imperial horses outside the Daming Gate; all attending ministers and the twenty-four carriage guides divide into left and right formations before the fasting hall and stand waiting.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the sacrifice, the responsible offices ready the imperial escort and the inner and outer guards. Officials who will take part in the rite line up in two ranks outside the Chongtian Gate. The Minister of Imperial Studs holds the imperial horses outside the Daming Gate. All attending ministers and the twenty-four carriage guides form left and right divisions before the fasting hall and await the procession.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍中跪奏請中嚴，俯伏興。

translations.literal: The Interpreter-in-Attendance leads the Palace Attendant to kneel and memorialize requesting the mid-watch vigil; he prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The Interpreter-in-Attendance escorts the Palace Attendant, who kneels and petitions for the mid-watch vigil to begin; he prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 少頃，侍中版奏外辦，皇帝即御座。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, the Palace Attendant reports on the memorial board that preparations outside are complete, and the emperor immediately takes his seat.
translations.idiomatic: After a short interval, the Palace Attendant announces on the memorial board that all is ready outside, and the emperor takes his seat at once.

sentences.zh: 四品以上應享執事官起居訖，侍中奏請升輿。

translations.literal: When ritual officials of the fourth rank and above who are to attend the offering have finished their bows of respect, the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that the emperor mount the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Once the officiating officials of fourth rank and above who will take part in the sacrifice have completed their bows of respect, the Palace Attendant petitions that the emperor mount the carriage.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出齋殿，降自正階，乘輿，華蓋傘扇如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor leaves the fasting hall, descends the main steps, mounts the imperial carriage, and the canopy, parasols, and fans proceed according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaves the fasting hall, descends the main steps, and mounts the imperial carriage; canopy, parasols, and fans are borne according to the usual ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 導駕官前導至大明門外，侍中進當輿前，奏請降輿，乘馬訖，導駕官分左右步導。

translations.literal: The carriage guides lead the way to outside the Daming Gate; the Palace Attendant advances before the carriage and memorializes requesting that the emperor dismount; when he has mounted his horse, the carriage guides walk on foot to guide him, dividing left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage guides lead the procession to the Daming Gate. The Palace Attendant steps forward before the carriage and petitions that the emperor dismount. Once he has mounted his horse, the guides walk on either side to conduct him forward.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎跪奏請進發，俯伏興，前稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Chancellery kneels and memorializes requesting departure; he prostrates himself and rises; ahead they call out to clear the way.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Chancellery kneels and petitions that the procession set out; he prostrates himself and rises, and heralds ahead call for the road to be cleared.

sentences.zh: 至崇天門，門下侍郎奏請權停，敕眾官上馬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the Chongtian Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery memorializes requesting a temporary halt and orders all officials to mount their horses.
translations.idiomatic: At the Chongtian Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery petitions for a brief halt and commands all officials to mount their horses.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨退，稱制可，門下侍郎退傳制，稱眾官上馬，贊者承傳，眾官出欞星門外，上馬訖，門下侍郎奏請進發，前稱警蹕，華蓋傘扇儀仗與眾官左右前引，教坊樂鼓吹不振作。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant receives the imperial command and withdraws, announcing that the decree is approved; the Vice Director of the Chancellery withdraws and transmits the decree, announcing that all officials are to mount; the announcer receives and relays it; all officials go outside the Spirit Star Gate, and when they have mounted, the Vice Director of the Chancellery memorializes requesting departure; ahead they call to clear the way; the canopy, parasols, fans, and ceremonial guards together with the officials lead forward on left and right; the Music Office drums and horns do not sound.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant receives the imperial command and withdraws, announcing that the decree is approved. The Vice Director of the Chancellery withdraws and transmits the order for all officials to mount. The announcer relays the command. The officials pass outside the Spirit Star Gate and mount their horses. The Vice Director of the Chancellery then petitions that the procession set out. Heralds ahead call for the road to be cleared. Canopy, parasols, fans, and ceremonial guards advance with the officials to left and right. The Music Office does not sound drums or horns.

sentences.zh: 至太廟欞星門外，紅橋南，贊者承傳眾官下馬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, south of the Red Bridge, the announcer receives and relays the command for all officials to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession reaches the area south of the Red Bridge, outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the announcer relays the command for all officials to dismount.

sentences.zh: 下馬訖，自卑而尊與儀仗倒卷而北，兩行駐立。

translations.literal: When they have dismounted, from low to high in rank and with the ceremonial guards folding back northward, they stand in two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have dismounted, officials array themselves from lowest to highest rank while the ceremonial guards fold back toward the north; all stand in two ranks.

sentences.zh: 駕至廟門，侍中奏請皇帝下馬，步入廟門。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reaches the temple gate, the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that the emperor dismount and enter the temple gate on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reaches the temple gate, the Palace Attendant petitions that the emperor dismount and enter the temple on foot.

sentences.zh: 入廟門訖，侍中奏請升輿，尚輦奉輿，華蓋傘扇如常儀。

translations.literal: When he has entered the temple gate, the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that he mount the carriage; the Director of Imperial Carriages presents the carriage; canopy, parasols, and fans proceed according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Once he has entered the temple gate, the Palace Attendant petitions that he mount the carriage again. The Director of Imperial Carriages presents the carriage, and canopy, parasols, and fans are borne according to the usual ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 導駕官前導，皇帝乘輿至大次前，侍中奏請降輿。

translations.literal: The carriage guides lead the way; the emperor rides in the carriage to before the grand tent, and the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that he dismount.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage guides lead the way as the emperor rides to the grand pavilion. The Palace Attendant petitions that he dismount.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降輿入就位，簾降，侍衛如式。

translations.literal: The emperor dismounts, enters, and takes his place; the curtain is lowered; the guards take their stations according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismounts, enters, and takes his place. The curtain is lowered and the guards assume their stations according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 尚食進膳，如常儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Victuals presents the meal, according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Victuals serves the meal, in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使以祝冊奏禦署訖，奉出，太廟令受之，各奠於坫，置各室祝案上。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies presents the prayer text for imperial signature; when this is complete, he carries it out; the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple receives it, places each on its altar mound, and sets them on the prayer tables in each chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies presents the prayer text for the emperor's signature. When the text has been signed, he carries it out. The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple receives it, places each copy on its altar mound, and sets them on the prayer tables in the respective chambers.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人承旨，敕眾官各還齋次。

translations.literal: The Interpreter-in-Attendance receives the imperial command and orders all officials each to return to their fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Interpreter-in-Attendance receives the imperial command and directs all officials to return to their fasting quarters.

sentences.zh: 四曰省牲器，見前親祀儀。

translations.literal: The fourth is inspecting the sacrificial victims and vessels; see the earlier ceremony for personal imperial sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth stage is the inspection of sacrificial victims and vessels, as described in the personal imperial sacrifice ceremony above.

sentences.zh: 五曰晨祼。

translations.literal: The fifth is the morning libation.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth stage is the morning libation.

sentences.zh: 享日醜前五刻，光祿卿、良醞令、太官令入實籩豆簠簋尊罍，各如常儀。

translations.literal: On the day of the offering, five quarters before the chou hour of the third watch, the Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, the Director of Fine Brew, and the Director of Imperial Kitchens fill the baskets, trays, grain vessels, and wine vessels, each according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the sacrifice, one hour and fifteen minutes before the chou hour, the Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, the Director of Fine Brew, and the Director of the Imperial Kitchens fill the baskets, trays, grain vessels, and wine vessels, each according to the usual procedure.

sentences.zh: 太樂令率工人二舞，以次入就位。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Music leads the artisans of the two dances to enter in order and take their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Music leads the performers of the two ritual dances to enter in order and take their stations.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引御史及執事者以次入就位。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants lead the Censor and officiants to enter in order and take their places.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants escort the Censor and officiating officials to enter in order and take their stations.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿、御史升殿點視陳設，退復位。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants lead the Minister of Imperial Rites and the Censor to ascend the hall and inspect the arrangement of offerings, then withdraw and return to their places.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants escort the Minister of Imperial Rites and the Censor up the hall to inspect the ritual furnishings, then withdraw and return to their stations.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒等官詣各室，分香設酒如常儀。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants lead the Minister of Education and other officials to each chamber to distribute incense and set out wine according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants escort the Minister of Education and other officials to each chamber to distribute incense and set out wine in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 禮直官復引太常卿及御史、太廟令、太祝、宮闈令升殿、奉出帝後神主訖，各退降就拜位，立定。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants again lead the Minister of Imperial Rites, the Censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Chief Sacrificer, and the Director of Palace Inner Quarters to ascend the hall and bring out the spirit tablets of the emperors and empresses; when this is complete, each withdraws, descends, takes his bowing place, and stands in position.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants again escort the Minister of Imperial Rites, the Censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Chief Sacrificer, and the Director of Palace Inner Quarters up the hall to bring out the spirit tablets of the emperors and empresses. When this is done, each withdraws, descends, takes his place for obeisance, and stands at attention.

sentences.zh: 奉禮於殿上贊奉神主訖，奉禮贊曰「再拜」，贊者承傳，御史以下皆再拜訖，各就位。

translations.literal: The Ritual Usher on the hall announces that the presentation of the spirit tablets is complete; the Ritual Usher announces, "Bow twice"; the announcer receives and relays it; from the Censor downward all bow twice; when this is complete, each takes his place.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall, the Ritual Usher announces that the spirit tablets have been presented. The Ritual Usher calls, "Bow twice," and the announcer relays the command. From the Censor downward, all perform the double bow, then each returns to his station.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引攝太尉由南神門東偏門入就位，立定。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants lead the Acting Grand Commandant to enter through the eastern side gate of the southern spirit gate and take his place; he stands in position.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants escort the Acting Grand Commandant in through the eastern side gate of the southern spirit gate to take his station and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 協律郎跪俯伏，舉麾興，工鼓，宮縣樂作《思成之曲》，以黃鐘為宮，大呂為角，太簇為徵，應鐘為羽，作文舞九成止。

translations.literal: The Pitch Master kneels and prostrates himself, raises the baton and rises; the artisans beat the drums; the palace ensemble performs the "Song of Reflective Completion," with the yellow bell as keynote, the great lü as second, the great cluster as third, and the responding bell as fifth; the civil dance is performed in nine sections and stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Pitch Master kneels and prostrates himself, raises his baton, and rises. The musicians strike the drums, and the palace ensemble performs the "Song of Reflective Completion," with the yellow bell as keynote, the great lü as second, the great cluster as third, and the responding bell as fifth. The civil dance runs through nine sections and concludes.

sentences.zh: 太尉以下皆再拜訖，禮直官引太尉詣盥洗位，宮縣樂作《肅寧之曲》，至位樂止，北向立，搢笏、盥手、帨手，執笏詣爵洗位，北向立，搢笏、洗瓚、拭瓚，以瓚授執事者。

translations.literal: When the Grand Commandant and those below have all bowed twice, the ritual attendants lead the Grand Commandant to the hand-washing place; the palace ensemble performs the "Song of Solemn Tranquility"; when he reaches his place the music stops; he stands facing north, inserts his tablet, washes his hands, and dries his hands; holding his tablet he goes to the libation-cup washing place, stands facing north, inserts his tablet, washes the libation cup, wipes the libation cup, and hands the cup to the officiant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Commandant and those below him have all completed the double bow, the ritual attendants escort the Grand Commandant to the hand-washing station. The palace ensemble plays the "Song of Solemn Tranquility." When he reaches his place, the music stops. He stands facing north, inserts his tablet, washes his hands, and dries them. Holding his tablet, he proceeds to the libation-cup washing station, stands facing north, inserts his tablet, washes and wipes the libation cup, and hands the cup to an officiant.

sentences.zh: 執笏升殿，宮縣樂作，至阼階下，樂止。

translations.literal: Holding his tablet he ascends the hall; the palace ensemble plays; when he reaches below the eastern steps, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: Tablet in hand, he ascends the hall while the palace ensemble plays. When he reaches the foot of the eastern steps, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 升自阼階，登歌樂作，詣太祖尊彜所，西向立，樂止。

translations.literal: He ascends by the eastern steps; the ascent music plays; he proceeds to where the wine vessels for Taizu are placed, stands facing west, and the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: He ascends the eastern steps as the ascent music plays, proceeds to where the wine vessels for Taizu are set out, stands facing west, and the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 執事者以瓚奉太尉，太尉搢笏執瓚。

translations.literal: The officiant presents the libation cup to the Grand Commandant; the Grand Commandant inserts his tablet and holds the cup.
translations.idiomatic: An officiant presents the libation cup to the Grand Commandant, who inserts his tablet and takes the cup.

sentences.zh: 司尊者舉冪酌郁鬯訖，太尉以瓚授執事者，執笏詣太祖神位前，搢笏跪，三上香，執事者以瓚奉太尉，太尉執瓚以鬯祼地訖，以虛瓚授執事者。

translations.literal: The wine steward lifts the covering and pours the aromatic ceremonial wine; when this is complete, the Grand Commandant hands the cup to the officiant; holding his tablet he proceeds before the spirit seat of Taizu, inserts his tablet and kneels, offers incense three times; the officiant presents the cup to the Grand Commandant; the Grand Commandant holds the cup and pours the aromatic wine as a libation on the ground; when this is complete, he hands the empty cup to the officiant.
translations.idiomatic: The wine steward lifts the covering and pours the aromatic ceremonial wine. The Grand Commandant hands the cup to an officiant, then, tablet in hand, proceeds before the spirit seat of Taizu, inserts his tablet, and kneels to offer incense three times. An officiant presents the cup again; the Grand Commandant pours the aromatic wine as a libation on the ground, then returns the empty cup to the officiant.

sentences.zh: 執笏俯伏興，退出戶外，北向再拜訖，次詣各室，並如上儀。

translations.literal: Holding his tablet he prostrates himself and rises, withdraws outside the door, faces north and bows twice; next he proceeds to each chamber, all according to the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: Tablet in hand, he prostrates himself and rises, withdraws outside the door, faces north, and performs the double bow. He then proceeds to each chamber in turn, following the same procedure throughout.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，降自阼階，復位。

translations.literal: When the ritual is complete, he descends by the eastern steps and returns to his place.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is finished, he descends the eastern steps and returns to his station.

sentences.zh: 六曰進饌。

translations.literal: The sixth is presenting the food offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth stage is the presentation of food offerings.

sentences.zh: 太尉祼將畢，進饌如前儀。

translations.literal: When the Grand Commandant's libation is nearly complete, the food offerings are presented as in the ritual above.
translations.idiomatic: As the Grand Commandant's libation nears completion, the food offerings are presented according to the procedure described above.

sentences.zh: 七曰酌獻。

translations.literal: The seventh is pouring and offering wine.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh stage is the pouring and offering of wine.

sentences.zh: 太尉既升祼，禮直官引博士，博士引禮儀使至大次前，北向立。

translations.literal: When the Grand Commandant has ascended to perform the libation, the ritual attendants lead the Erudite; the Erudite leads the Master of Ceremonies to before the grand tent, where they stand facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Grand Commandant has ascended to perform the libation, the ritual attendants escort the Erudite, who in turn escorts the Master of Ceremonies to the grand pavilion, where they stand facing north.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍中詣大次前，版奏請中嚴，皇帝服袞冕。

translations.literal: The Interpreter-in-Attendance leads the Palace Attendant to before the grand tent; he reports on the memorial board requesting the mid-watch vigil; the emperor dons his sacrificial robes and cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Interpreter-in-Attendance escorts the Palace Attendant to the grand pavilion, where he announces on the memorial board that the mid-watch vigil is to begin. The emperor puts on his sacrificial robes and cap.

sentences.zh: 坐少頃，侍中奏外辦，禮儀使跪奏請皇帝行禮，俯伏興。

translations.literal: After sitting a short while, the Palace Attendant memorializes that preparations outside are complete; the Master of Ceremonies kneels and memorializes requesting that the emperor perform the ritual; he prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: After a brief interval, the Palace Attendant announces that all is ready outside. The Master of Ceremonies kneels and petitions that the emperor proceed with the rite, then prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 簾卷出次，禮儀使前導至西神門，華蓋傘扇停於門外，近侍從入，太禮使後從。

translations.literal: The curtain is raised and he leaves the tent; the Master of Ceremonies leads the way to the western spirit gate; canopy, parasols, and fans halt outside the gate; close attendants follow in; the Grand Master of Rites follows behind.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain is raised and the emperor leaves the pavilion. The Master of Ceremonies leads the way to the western spirit gate. Canopy, parasols, and fans remain outside the gate. Close attendants enter with him, and the Grand Master of Rites follows behind.

sentences.zh: 殿中監跪進鎮圭，皇帝執圭入門，協律郎跪，俯伏興，舉麾，宮縣《順成之樂》作，至版位東向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Bureau kneels and presents the ceremonial jade tablet; the emperor holds the tablet and enters the gate; the Pitch Master kneels, prostrates himself and rises, raises the baton; the palace ensemble performs the "Music of Smooth Completion"; when he reaches the memorial board place he stands facing east; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Bureau kneels and presents the ceremonial jade tablet. The emperor takes the tablet and enters the gate. The Pitch Master kneels, prostrates himself, rises, and raises his baton. The palace ensemble performs the "Music of Smooth Completion." When the emperor reaches the memorial board station and stands facing east, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 引禮官分左右侍立，禮儀使奏請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual guides stand attending on left and right; the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that the emperor bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual guides stand in attendance to left and right. The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor perform the double bow.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「眾官再拜」，贊者承傳，凡在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Ritual Usher says, "All officials bow twice"; the announcer receives and relays it; all who are in position bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Usher calls, "All officials, bow twice." The announcer relays the command, and everyone in attendance performs the double bow.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝詣盥洗位，宮縣樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that the emperor proceed to the hand-washing place; the palace ensemble plays; when he reaches his place the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor proceed to the hand-washing station. The palace ensemble plays until he reaches his place, then the music stops.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪取醿，興，沃水，又內侍跪取盤，承水。

translations.literal: A palace attendant kneels, takes the pitcher, rises, and pours water; another palace attendant kneels, takes the basin, and receives the water.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant kneels, takes the pitcher, rises, and pours water. Another palace attendant kneels, takes the basin, and catches the water.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，皇帝搢圭盥手。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he insert the ceremonial jade tablet; the emperor inserts the tablet and washes his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor insert the ceremonial jade tablet. The emperor inserts the tablet and washes his hands.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪取巾於篚，興，進。

translations.literal: A palace attendant kneels, takes the towel from the basket, rises, and advances.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant kneels, takes the towel from the basket, rises, and presents it.

sentences.zh: 帨手訖，奉爵官以爵跪進。

translations.literal: When he has dried his hands, the officer presenting the libation cup kneels and advances with the cup.
translations.idiomatic: Once his hands are dried, the officer who presents the libation cup kneels and advances with the cup.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受爵，內侍奉醿沃水，又內侍奉盤承水。

translations.literal: The emperor receives the cup; a palace attendant presents the pitcher and pours water; another palace attendant presents the basin and receives the water.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor receives the cup. A palace attendant presents the pitcher and pours water; another presents the basin and catches the water.

sentences.zh: 皇帝洗爵訖，內侍奉巾跪進。

translations.literal: When the emperor has finished washing the cup, a palace attendant kneels and presents the towel.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor has finished washing the cup, a palace attendant kneels and presents the towel.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拭爵訖，內侍奠盤醿，又奠巾於篚，奉爵官受爵。

translations.literal: When the emperor has finished wiping the cup, a palace attendant sets down the basin and pitcher; he sets the towel back in the basket; the officer presenting the cup receives the cup.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor has finished wiping the cup, a palace attendant sets down the basin and pitcher and returns the towel to the basket. The officer who presents the cup takes the cup back.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，導升殿，宮縣樂作，至西階下，樂止。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he hold the ceremonial jade tablet and leads him to ascend the hall; the palace ensemble plays; when he reaches below the western steps, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take up the ceremonial jade tablet and leads him up the hall while the palace ensemble plays. When he reaches the foot of the western steps, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 升自西階，登歌樂作。

translations.literal: He ascends by the western steps; the ascent music plays.
translations.idiomatic: He ascends the western steps as the ascent music plays.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前導詣太祖室尊彜所，東向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way to where the wine vessels are placed in the chamber of Taizu; he stands facing east; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way to where the wine vessels are set out in the chamber of Taizu. The emperor stands facing east, and the music ceases.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，奏《開成之曲》，奉爵官以爵蒞尊，執事者舉冪，侍中跪酌犧尊之泛齊，以爵授執事者。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble plays and performs the "Song of Opening Completion"; the officer presenting the cup brings the cup to the wine vessel; the officiant lifts the covering; the Palace Attendant kneels and pours the first fermentation from the sacrificial vessel; he hands the cup to the officiant.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble plays the "Song of Opening Completion." The officer who presents the cup brings it to the wine vessel. An officiant lifts the covering. The Palace Attendant kneels and pours the first fermentation from the sacrificial vessel, then hands the cup to an officiant.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前導，入詣太祖神位前，北向立。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way, enters, and proceeds before the spirit seat of Taizu, where he stands facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way into the chamber and proceeds before the spirit seat of Taizu, where the emperor stands facing north.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，跪，又奏請三上香。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he insert the ceremonial jade tablet and kneel; he again memorializes requesting that incense be offered three times.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor insert the ceremonial jade tablet and kneel, then petitions that incense be offered three times.

sentences.zh: 上香訖，奉爵官以爵授進酒官，進酒官東向以爵跪進，禮儀使奏請執爵祭酒。

translations.literal: When the incense offering is complete, the officer presenting the cup hands the cup to the wine-offering officer; the wine-offering officer, facing east, kneels and advances with the cup; the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he take the cup and offer libation wine.
translations.idiomatic: When the incense offering is complete, the officer who presents the cup hands it to the wine-offering officer, who kneels facing east and advances with the cup. The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take the cup and offer libation wine.

sentences.zh: 執爵三祭酒於茅苴訖，以虛爵授進酒官，進酒官受爵以授奉爵官，退立尊彜所。

translations.literal: Holding the cup he offers libation wine three times on the thatch bundle; when this is complete he hands the empty cup to the wine-offering officer; the wine-offering officer receives the cup and hands it to the officer presenting the cup; he withdraws and stands where the wine vessels are placed.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the cup, the emperor pours libation wine three times on the thatch bundle. He then hands the empty cup to the wine-offering officer, who passes it to the officer who presents the cup and withdraws to stand by the wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 進酒官進徹神案上所奠玉爵馬湩，東向跪進，禮儀使奏請執爵祭馬湩。

translations.literal: The wine-offering officer advances and removes the jade cup of kumiss set on the spirit table; kneeling and facing east he advances; the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he take the cup and offer libation of kumiss.
translations.idiomatic: The wine-offering officer advances and takes up the jade cup of kumiss set on the spirit table, kneels facing east, and presents it. The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take the cup and offer libation of kumiss.

sentences.zh: 祭訖以虛爵授進酒官，進酒官進奠神案上訖，退。

translations.literal: When the libation is complete he hands the empty cup to the wine-offering officer; the wine-offering officer advances and sets it on the spirit table; when this is complete he withdraws.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation is complete, he hands the empty cup to the wine-offering officer, who sets it back on the spirit table and withdraws.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執圭，俯伏興，司徒搢笏跪俎前，舉牲盤西向以進。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he hold the jade tablet; he prostrates himself and rises; the Minister of Education inserts his tablet, kneels before the meat stand, lifts the sacrificial tray facing west, and advances.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take up the jade tablet. The emperor prostrates himself and rises. The Minister of Education inserts his tablet, kneels before the meat stand, lifts the sacrificial tray facing west, and advances.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，皇帝搢圭，俯受牲盤，北向跪，奠神案上訖，禮儀奏請執圭興，前導出戶外褥位，北向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he insert the ceremonial jade tablet; the emperor inserts the tablet, bows to receive the sacrificial tray, kneels facing north, and sets it on the spirit table; when this is complete the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he hold the tablet and rise; he leads the way out to the mat place outside the door, stands facing north, and the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor insert the ceremonial jade tablet. The emperor inserts the tablet, bows to receive the sacrificial tray, kneels facing north, and sets it on the spirit table. The Master of Ceremonies then petitions that he take up the tablet and rise, leads him out to the mat station outside the door, where he stands facing north as the music stops.

sentences.zh: 舉祝官搢笏跪，對舉祝版。

translations.literal: The officer raising the prayer text inserts his tablet, kneels, and lifts the prayer board facing it.
translations.idiomatic: The officer who raises the prayer text inserts his tablet, kneels, and lifts the prayer board to face the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 讀祝官北向跪，讀祝文訖，俯伏興。

translations.literal: The officer reading the prayer text kneels facing north, reads the prayer text; when this is complete he prostrates himself and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The officer who reads the prayer text kneels facing north and recites the prayer. When he has finished, he prostrates himself and rises.

sentences.zh: 舉祝官奠祝版訖。

translations.literal: The officer raising the prayer text sets down the prayer board; when this is complete.
translations.idiomatic: The officer who raised the prayer text sets the board back in place.

sentences.zh: 先詣次室。

translations.literal: He first proceeds to the secondary chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeds first to the secondary chamber.

sentences.zh: 次蒙古祝史詣室前致祠訖，禮儀使奏請再拜。

translations.literal: Next the Mongol prayer scribe proceeds before the chamber and completes the offering prayer; the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting the double bow.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Mongol prayer scribe proceeds before the chamber and completes the offering prayer. The Master of Ceremonies petitions for the double bow.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，禮儀使前導詣各室，奏各室之樂。

translations.literal: When the bow is complete, the Master of Ceremonies leads the way to each chamber and the music for each chamber is performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow is complete, the Master of Ceremonies leads the way to each chamber in turn, and the music appropriate to each chamber is performed.

sentences.zh: 其酌獻、進牲體、祭馬湩，並如第一室之儀。

translations.literal: The pouring and offering of wine, presentation of sacrificial meat, and libation of kumiss are all according to the ritual of the first chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The pouring and offering of wine, presentation of sacrificial meat, and libation of kumiss follow the same procedure as in the first chamber.

sentences.zh: 既畢，禮儀使奏請詣飲福位。

translations.literal: When this is complete, the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he proceed to the place for drinking the blessing wine.
translations.idiomatic: When this is complete, the Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor proceed to the station for drinking the blessing wine.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，至位，西向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The ascent music plays; when he reaches his place he stands facing west; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent music plays. When he reaches his station, he stands facing west, and the music stops.

sentences.zh: 宮縣《釐成之樂》作，禮直官引司徒立於飲福位側，太祝以爵酌上尊福酒，合置一爵，以奉侍中，侍中受爵奉以立。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble performs the "Music of Ordered Completion"; the ritual attendants lead the Minister of Education to stand beside the place for drinking the blessing wine; the Chief Sacrificer pours the superior blessing wine with the cup, combines it in one cup, and presents it to the Palace Attendant; the Palace Attendant receives the cup and holds it standing.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble performs the "Music of Ordered Completion." The ritual attendants escort the Minister of Education to stand beside the blessing-wine station. The Chief Sacrificer pours the superior blessing wine into a single cup and presents it to the Palace Attendant, who receives the cup and stands holding it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that the emperor bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor perform the double bow.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，奏搢鎮圭跪，侍中東向以爵跪進。

translations.literal: When the bow is complete, he memorializes requesting that the emperor insert the ceremonial jade tablet and kneel; the Palace Attendant, facing east, kneels and advances with the cup.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow is complete, the Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor insert the ceremonial jade tablet and kneel. The Palace Attendant, facing east, kneels and advances with the cup.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執爵三祭酒，又奏請啐酒。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he take the cup and offer libation wine three times; he again memorializes requesting that he taste the wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take the cup and pour libation wine three times, then petitions that he taste the wine.

sentences.zh: 啐訖，以爵授侍中。

translations.literal: When he has tasted the wine, he hands the cup to the Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When he has tasted the wine, he hands the cup back to the Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請受胙，太祝以黍稷飯籩授司徒，司徒東向跪進，皇帝受，以授左右。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he receive the sacrificial meat; the Chief Sacrificer hands the basket of millet and glutinous grain to the Minister of Education; the Minister of Education, facing east, kneels and advances; the emperor receives it and hands it to attendants on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor receive the sacrificial portion. The Chief Sacrificer hands the basket of millet and glutinous grain to the Minister of Education, who kneels facing east and presents it. The emperor receives it and passes it to attendants on either side.

sentences.zh: 太祝又以胙肉俎跪授司徒，司徒跪進，皇帝受，以授左右，禮直官引司徒退立。

translations.literal: The Chief Sacrificer again kneels and hands the stand of sacrificial meat to the Minister of Education; the Minister of Education kneels and advances; the emperor receives it and hands it to attendants on left and right; the ritual attendants lead the Minister of Education to withdraw and stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Sacrificer again kneels and presents the stand of sacrificial meat to the Minister of Education, who kneels and advances it. The emperor receives it and passes it to attendants on either side. The ritual attendants then escort the Minister of Education back to his station.

sentences.zh: 侍中再以爵酒跪進，禮儀使奏請皇帝受爵，飲福酒訖，侍中受虛爵興，以授太祝。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant again kneels and advances with the cup of wine; the Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that the emperor receive the cup; when he has finished drinking the blessing wine, the Palace Attendant receives the empty cup, rises, and hands it to the Chief Sacrificer.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant again kneels and presents the cup of wine. The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor receive the cup and drink the blessing wine. When he has finished, the Palace Attendant takes the empty cup, rises, and hands it to the Chief Sacrificer.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，俯伏興，又奏請再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he hold the ceremonial jade tablet; he prostrates himself and rises; he again memorializes requesting the double bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor take up the ceremonial jade tablet. The emperor prostrates himself and rises. The Master of Ceremonies then petitions for the double bow.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bow is complete, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow is complete, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前導還版位。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way back to the memorial board place.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies leads the way back to the memorial board station.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，降自西階，樂止。

translations.literal: The ascent music plays; he descends by the western steps; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent music plays as he descends the western steps, then the music stops.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble plays; when he reaches his place the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble plays until he reaches his station, then the music stops.

sentences.zh: 奉禮於殿上唱太祝徹籩豆。

translations.literal: The Ritual Usher on the hall announces that the Chief Sacrificer is to remove the baskets and trays.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall, the Ritual Usher calls for the Chief Sacrificer to remove the baskets and trays.

sentences.zh: 宮縣《豐寧之樂》作，卒徹，樂止。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble performs the "Music of Abundant Tranquility"; when the removal is complete, the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble performs the "Music of Abundant Tranquility." When the removal is complete, the music stops.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「賜胙」，贊者唱「眾官再拜」，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Ritual Usher says, "The sacrificial meat is bestowed"; the announcer calls, "All officials bow twice"; all who are in position bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Usher announces, "The sacrificial portion is bestowed." The announcer calls, "All officials, bow twice," and everyone in attendance performs the double bow.

sentences.zh: 送神樂作，《保成之曲》作，一成止。

translations.literal: The music for escorting the spirits plays; the "Song of Preserved Completion" is performed in one section and stops.
translations.idiomatic: The music for escorting the spirits begins. The "Song of Preserved Completion" is performed in one section and concludes.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝再拜，贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that the emperor bow twice; the announcer receives and relays it; all who are in position bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor perform the double bow. The announcer relays the command, and everyone in attendance bows twice.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，禮儀使前奏禮畢，皇帝還大次。

translations.literal: When the bow is complete, the Master of Ceremonies advances and memorializes that the ritual is complete; the emperor returns to the grand tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow is complete, the Master of Ceremonies advances and announces that the rite is finished. The emperor returns to the grand pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宮縣《昌寧之樂》作，出門，樂止。

translations.literal: The palace ensemble performs the 《Music of Flourishing Tranquility》; he goes out the gate; the music stops.
translations.idiomatic: The palace ensemble performs the 《Music of Flourishing Tranquility》 as the emperor leaves the gate, then the music stops.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請釋鎮圭，殿中監跪受，華蓋傘扇如常儀。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies memorializes requesting that he release the ceremonial jade tablet; the Director of the Palace Bureau kneels and receives it; canopy, parasols, and fans proceed according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies petitions that the emperor release the ceremonial jade tablet. The Director of the Palace Bureau kneels and receives it. Canopy, parasols, and fans are borne according to the usual ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 入次，簾降。

translations.literal: He enters the tent; the curtain is lowered.
translations.idiomatic: He enters the pavilion and the curtain is lowered.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿、御史、太廟令、太祝、宮闈令升殿納神主訖，各降就位。

translations.literal: The ritual attendants lead the Minister of Imperial Rites, the Censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Chief Sacrificer, and the Director of Palace Inner Quarters to ascend the hall and return the spirit tablets; when this is complete each descends and takes his place.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendants escort the Minister of Imperial Rites, the Censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Chief Sacrificer, and the Director of Palace Inner Quarters up the hall to return the spirit tablets. When this is done, each descends and returns to his station.

sentences.zh: 贊者於殿上唱升納神主訖，奉禮曰「再拜」，御史以下諸執事者皆再拜訖，以次出。

translations.literal: The announcer on the hall calls that the spirit tablets have been returned; the Ritual Usher says, "Bow twice"; from the Censor downward all officiants bow twice; when this is complete they withdraw in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall, the announcer calls that the spirit tablets have been returned. The Ritual Usher calls, "Bow twice," and from the Censor downward all officiants perform the double bow, then withdraw in order.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人、禮直官各引享官以次出，太樂令率工人二舞以次出，太廟令闔戶訖降乃退。

translations.literal: The Interpreter-in-Attendance and ritual attendants each lead the offering officials to withdraw in order; the Director of Imperial Music leads the artisans of the two dances to withdraw in order; the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple closes the doors and withdraws only after descending.
translations.idiomatic: The Interpreter-in-Attendance and ritual attendants escort the offering officials out in order. The Director of Imperial Music leads the performers of the two dances out in order. The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple closes the doors and withdraws only after descending.

sentences.zh: 祝版藏於匱。

translations.literal: The prayer boards are stored in the chest.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer boards are placed in the chest for storage.

sentences.zh: 八曰車駕還宮。

translations.literal: The eighth is the imperial procession returning to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth stage is the emperor's return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既還大次，侍中奏請解嚴。

translations.literal: When the emperor has returned to the grand tent, the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that the vigil be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor has returned to the grand pavilion, the Palace Attendant petitions that the vigil be lifted.

sentences.zh: 皇帝釋衮冕，停大次。

translations.literal: The emperor removes his sacrificial robes and cap and remains in the grand tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removes his sacrificial robes and cap and remains in the grand pavilion.

sentences.zh: 五刻頃，尚食進膳，如常儀。

translations.literal: At about the fifth quarter-watch, the Director of Imperial Victuals presents the meal, according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At about the fifth quarter-watch, the Director of Imperial Victuals serves the meal in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 所司備儀從、內外仗，與從祀諸執事官兩行序立太廟欞星門外。

translations.literal: The responsible offices prepare the retinue and inner and outer guards; officials attending the sacrifice stand in two ranks outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices ready the imperial escort and the inner and outer guards. Officials who took part in the sacrifice line up in two ranks outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏外辦，皇帝出次升輿，導駕官前導，華蓋傘扇如常儀。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reports on the memorial board that preparations outside are complete; the emperor leaves the tent and mounts the carriage; the carriage guides lead the way; canopy, parasols, and fans proceed according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announces on the memorial board that all is ready outside. The emperor leaves the pavilion and mounts the carriage. The carriage guides lead the way, and canopy, parasols, and fans are borne according to the usual ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 至廟門，太僕卿進御馬，侍中奏請皇帝降輿乘馬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the temple gate, the Minister of Imperial Studs presents the imperial horses; the Palace Attendant memorializes requesting that the emperor dismount and mount a horse.
translations.idiomatic: At the temple gate, the Minister of Imperial Studs presents the imperial horses. The Palace Attendant petitions that the emperor dismount and mount a horse.

sentences.zh: 乘馬訖，門下侍郎奏請進發，俯伏興退，前稱警蹕。

translations.literal: When he has mounted, the Vice Director of the Chancellery memorializes requesting departure; he prostrates himself, rises, and withdraws; ahead they call to clear the way.
translations.idiomatic: Once he has mounted, the Vice Director of the Chancellery petitions that the procession set out, prostrates himself, rises, and withdraws. Heralds ahead call for the road to be cleared.

sentences.zh: 至欞星門外，門下侍郎奏請權停，敕眾官上馬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching outside the Spirit Star Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery memorializes requesting a temporary halt and orders all officials to mount their horses.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Spirit Star Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery petitions for a brief halt and commands all officials to mount their horses.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨退稱曰「制可」，門下侍郎退傳制，贊者承傳，眾官上馬畢，導駕官及華蓋傘扇分左右前導，稱警蹕，教坊樂鼓吹振作。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant receives the imperial command, withdraws, and announces, "The decree is approved"; the Vice Director of the Chancellery withdraws and transmits the decree; the announcer receives and relays it; when all officials have mounted, the carriage guides together with canopy, parasols, and fans lead forward on left and right, calling to clear the way; the Music Office drums and horns sound.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant receives the imperial command, withdraws, and announces, "The decree is approved." The Vice Director of the Chancellery withdraws and transmits the order. The announcer relays it. When all officials have mounted, the carriage guides advance with canopy, parasols, and fans to left and right, calling for the road to be cleared. The Music Office sounds drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 至崇天門欞星門外，門下侍郎奏請權停，敕眾官下馬。

translations.literal: Upon reaching outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Chongtian Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery memorializes requesting a temporary halt and orders all officials to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Spirit Star Gate of the Chongtian Gate, the Vice Director of the Chancellery petitions for a brief halt and commands all officials to dismount.

sentences.zh: 贊者承傳，眾官下馬訖，左右前引入內石橋北，與儀仗倒卷而北，駐立。

translations.literal: The announcer receives and relays the command; when all officials have dismounted, they are led forward on left and right to the north of the inner stone bridge; with the ceremonial guards folding back northward, they stand in place.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer relays the command. Once all officials have dismounted, they are conducted forward to the north of the inner stone bridge. The ceremonial guards fold back toward the north, and all stand in place.

sentences.zh: 駕入崇天門，至大明門外降馬，升輿以入，駕既入，通事舍人承旨敕眾官皆退，宿衛官率衛士宿衛如式。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage enters the Chongtian Gate; at outside the Daming Gate he dismounts and mounts the carriage to enter; when the carriage has entered, the Interpreter-in-Attendance receives the imperial command and orders all officials to withdraw; the guard officers lead the guards to stand night watch according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage enters the Chongtian Gate. Outside the Daming Gate the emperor dismounts and mounts the carriage to enter. Once the carriage has entered, the Interpreter-in-Attendance receives the imperial command and directs all officials to withdraw. Guard officers lead the guards to take up night watch according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 攝祀儀，其目有九：

translations.literal: The ceremony for proxy sacrifice—its categories number nine:
translations.idiomatic: The proxy sacrifice ceremony comprises nine stages:

sentences.zh: 一曰齋戒。

translations.literal: The first is purification and abstention.
translations.idiomatic: The first stage is ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 享前三日，三獻官以下凡與祭員，皆公服受誓戒於中書省。

translations.literal: Three days before the offering, all participants from the three offering officers downward, wearing official dress, receive the abstention oath at the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the sacrifice, everyone from the three offering officers downward who will take part, in official dress, receive the purification oath at the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是日質明，有司設金椅於省庭，一人執紅羅傘立於其左。

translations.literal: On that day at dawn, the responsible offices set out a golden chair in the courtyard of the Secretariat; one person holds a red silk parasol and stands to its left.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day, the responsible offices place a golden chair in the Secretariat courtyard, with an attendant holding a red silk parasol to its left.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎率儀鸞局陳設版位，獻官諸執事位，俱藉以席，仍加紫綾褥。

translations.literal: The Ritual Gentleman leads the Ceremonial Escort Bureau in setting out the memorial board places and the places for offering officials and various officiants; all are spread with mats and further covered with purple silk cushions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Gentleman leads the Ceremonial Escort Bureau in arranging the memorial board stations and the stations for offering officials and other officiants, each spread with mats and covered with purple silk cushions.

sentences.zh: 設初獻太尉位於省階少西，南向；

translations.literal: The place for the Chief Offering Officer, Acting Grand Commandant, is set on the western side of the Secretariat steps, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Chief Offering Officer, the Acting Grand Commandant, is placed slightly west of the Secretariat steps, facing south;

sentences.zh: 大禮使位於其東，少南，西向；

translations.literal: The place for the Grand Master of Rites is set to its east, slightly south, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Grand Master of Rites is placed to its east, slightly to the south, facing west;

sentences.zh: 監祭御史位二，於通道之西，東向；

translations.literal: Two places for the Supervising Sacrifice Censor are set on the west of the passage, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Two stations for the Supervising Sacrifice Censor are placed west of the passage, facing east;

sentences.zh: 監禮博士位二，於通道之東，西向；

translations.literal: Two places for the Supervising Ritual Erudite are set on the east of the passage, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: Two stations for the Supervising Ritual Erudite are placed east of the passage, facing west;

sentences.zh: 俱北上。

translations.literal: All with north as the superior direction.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the northern position is superior.

sentences.zh: 設司徒亞終獻位於其南，北向，西上。

translations.literal: The places for the Minister of Education as secondary and final offering officers are set to their south, facing north, with west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the Minister of Education as secondary and final offering officers are placed to the south, facing north, with the western position superior.

sentences.zh: 次助奠七祀獻官，次太常卿、光祿卿、光祿丞、書祝官、讀祝官、太官令、良醞令、廩犧令、司尊彜、舉祝官、太官丞、廩犧丞、奉爵官、奉瓚官、盥爵官二、巾篚官、蒙古太祝、巫祝、點視儀衛、清道官及與祭官，依品級陳設，皆異位重行。

translations.literal: Next come the seven subsidiary offering officers for the seven sacrifices, then the Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, prayer-writing officer, prayer-reading officer, Director of Imperial Kitchens, Director of Fine Brew, Director of Sacrificial Livestock, wine-vessel steward, prayer-board officer, Vice Director of Imperial Kitchens, Vice Director of Sacrificial Livestock, cup-presenting officer, libation-cup-presenting officer, two cup-washing officers, towel-and-basket officer, Mongol Chief Sacrificer, shaman sacrificer, ritual guard inspector, road-clearing officer, and participating officials—arranged according to rank, each in a separate place in double ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Next come the seven subsidiary offering officers for the seven sacrifices, followed by the Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, prayer-writing officer, prayer-reading officer, Director of the Imperial Kitchens, Director of Fine Brew, Director of Sacrificial Livestock, wine-vessel steward, prayer-board officer, Vice Director of the Imperial Kitchens, Vice Director of Sacrificial Livestock, cup-presenting officer, libation-cup-presenting officer, two cup-washing officers, towel-and-basket officer, Mongol Chief Sacrificer, shaman sacrificer, ritual guard inspector, road-clearing officer, and all other participating officials—each placed according to rank in separate stations arranged in double ranks.

sentences.zh: 太廟令、太樂令、郊社令、太祝位於通道之西，北向，東上。

translations.literal: The places for the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of Imperial Music, Director of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices, and Chief Sacrificer are set on the west of the passage, facing north, with east as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of Imperial Music, Director of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices, and Chief Sacrificer are placed west of the passage, facing north, with the eastern position superior.

sentences.zh: 太廟丞、太樂丞、郊社丞、奉禮郎、協律郎、司天生位於通道之東，北向，西上。

translations.literal: The places for the Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Vice Director of Imperial Music, Vice Director of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices, Ritual Gentleman, Pitch Master, and Director of Natural Sounds are set on the east of the passage, facing north, with west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Vice Director of Imperial Music, Vice Director of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices, Ritual Gentleman, Pitch Master, and Director of Natural Sounds are placed east of the passage, facing north, with the western position superior.

sentences.zh: 齋郎位於其後。

translations.literal: The places for the fasting officers are set behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the fasting officers are placed behind them.

sentences.zh: 贊者引行事等官，各就位，立定。

translations.literal: The announcer leads the officiating officials and others each to his place; they stand in position.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer escorts the officiating officials and others to their respective stations, where they stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 次引初獻官立定。

translations.literal: Next the announcer leads the chief offering officer to stand in position.
translations.idiomatic: Next the announcer escorts the chief offering officer to his station.

sentences.zh: 禮直官搢笏，讀誓文曰「某年某月某日，享於太廟，各揚其職，其或不敬，國有常刑」。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant inserts his tablet and reads the oath text: "On such-and-such a year, month, and day, an offering is made at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Each shall perform his duty; whoever is not reverent shall be punished according to the statutes of the state."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendant inserts his tablet and reads the oath: "On such-and-such a year, month, and day, an offering is made at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Each shall perform his duty; whoever is not reverent shall be punished according to the statutes of the state."

sentences.zh: 散齋二日宿於正寢，致齋一日宿於祠所。

translations.literal: For preliminary abstention he lodges two days in the main quarters; for strict abstention he lodges one day at the place of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: During preliminary fasting he lodges two days in the main quarters; during strict fasting he lodges one day at the sacrificial site.

sentences.zh: 散齋日治事如故，不吊喪問病，不作樂，不判署刑殺文字，不決罰罪人，不與穢惡事。

translations.literal: On days of preliminary abstention he conducts affairs as usual, but does not offer condolences or inquire after the ill, does not make music, does not sign documents involving capital punishment, does not pass sentence on criminals, and does not engage in defiling or impure matters.
translations.idiomatic: On days of preliminary fasting he conducts affairs as usual, but does not offer condolences or inquire after the ill, make music, sign documents involving capital punishment, pass sentence on criminals, or engage in defiling or impure matters.

sentences.zh: 致齋日惟享事得行，余悉禁。

translations.literal: On days of strict abstention only sacrificial affairs may be conducted; all else is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On days of strict fasting only sacrificial affairs may be conducted; everything else is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 凡與享之官，已齋而闕者，通攝行事。

translations.literal: For any official taking part in the offering who has observed abstention but is absent, another shall comprehensively act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: If an official who has completed fasting is absent from the sacrifice, another shall act comprehensively in his stead.

sentences.zh: 七品以下官先退，余官再拜。

translations.literal: Officials of the seventh rank and below withdraw first; the remaining officials bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the seventh rank and below withdraw first; the remaining officials perform the double bow.

sentences.zh: 禮直官贊「鞠躬」，「拜」，「興」，「拜」，「興」，「平立」，「禮畢」。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant announces "Bow the body," "Bow," "Rise," "Bow," "Rise," "Stand level," "The ritual is complete."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendant calls "Bow the body," "Bow," "Rise," "Bow," "Rise," "Stand level," and "The ritual is complete."

sentences.zh: 守廟兵衛與太樂工人，俱清齋一宿。

translations.literal: The temple guards and the artisans of Imperial Music all observe pure fasting for one night.
translations.idiomatic: The temple guards and the artisans of Imperial Music all observe pure fasting for one night.

sentences.zh: 赴祝所之日，官給酒饌。

translations.literal: On the day of proceeding to the prayer-writing place, the court supplies wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of proceeding to the prayer-writing place, the court supplies wine and food.

sentences.zh: 二曰陳設。

translations.literal: The second is arranging the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The second stage is the arrangement of ritual furnishings.

sentences.zh: 享前二日，所司設兵衛於廟門，禁斷行人。

translations.literal: Two days before the offering, the responsible offices post military guards at the temple gate and forbid passage to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before the sacrifice, the responsible offices post military guards at the temple gate and forbid travelers to pass.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞局設幄幔於饌殿，所司設三獻官以下行事執事官次於齋房之所。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Escort Bureau sets curtains in the food-preparation hall; the responsible offices set places for the three offering officers and other officiating officials in the fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Escort Bureau hangs curtains in the food-preparation hall, and the responsible offices arrange quarters for the three offering officers and other officiating officials in the fasting rooms.

sentences.zh: 前一日，太樂令率其屬設宮縣之樂於庭中。

translations.literal: On the previous day, the Director of Imperial Music leads his subordinates to set up the palace ensemble music in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the sacrifice, the Director of Imperial Music leads his subordinates to set up the palace ensemble in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 東方西方磬虡起北，鐘虡次之；

translations.literal: On the east and west, the stone chime frames begin from the north, with bell frames next;
translations.idiomatic: On the east and west, the stone chime frames begin from the north, with the bell frames placed next;

sentences.zh: 南主北方磬虡起西，鐘虡次之。

translations.literal: On the south and north, the stone chime frames for south and north begin from the west, with bell frames next.
translations.idiomatic: On the south and north, the stone chime frames begin from the west, with the bell frames placed next.

sentences.zh: 設十二镈鐘於編縣之間。

translations.literal: Twelve bozhong bells are set among the suspended frames.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bozhong bells are set among the suspended frames.

sentences.zh: 各依辰位。

translations.literal: Each is placed according to its earthly branch position.
translations.idiomatic: Each is placed according to its position in the cycle of earthly branches.

sentences.zh: 樹建鼓於四隅，置敔於北縣之內。

translations.literal: Standing drums are erected at the four corners; a wooden tiger is placed inside the northern frame.
translations.idiomatic: Standing drums are erected at the four corners, and a wooden tiger drum is placed inside the northern frame.

sentences.zh: 一在道東，一在道西。

translations.literal: One is east of the path, one west of the path.
translations.idiomatic: One stands east of the path and one west of the path.

sentences.zh: 路鼓一在之東南，晉鼓一在其後，又路鼓一在之西南。

translations.literal: One road drum is southeast of it, one Jin drum behind it, and another road drum southwest of it.
translations.idiomatic: One road drum stands to its southeast, one Jin drum behind it, and another road drum to its southwest.

sentences.zh: 諸工人各於其後。

translations.literal: The various artisans each stand behind their instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Each artisan stands behind his instrument.

sentences.zh: 東方西方，以北為上；

translations.literal: On the east and west, north is superior;
translations.idiomatic: On the east and west, the northern position is superior;

sentences.zh: 南方北方，以西為上。

translations.literal: On the south and north, west is superior.
translations.idiomatic: On the south and north, the western position is superior.

sentences.zh: 文舞在北，武舞在南，立舞表於酂綴之間。

translations.literal: The civil dance is in the north, the martial dance in the south; standing dancers are marked between the zan and zhui markers.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance is in the north and the martial dance in the south; standing dancers are marked between the zan and zhui markers.

sentences.zh: 又設登歌之樂於殿上前楹間。

translations.literal: The ascent music is also set between the front pillars of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent music is also set between the front pillars of the hall.

sentences.zh: 玉磬一虡在西，金鐘一虡在東，一在金鐘北稍西，一在玉磬北稍東。

translations.literal: One jade chime frame is in the west, one golden bell frame in the east; one is slightly west of the golden bell, one slightly east of the jade chime.
translations.idiomatic: One jade chime frame stands in the west and one golden bell frame in the east; one is placed slightly west of the golden bell and one slightly east of the jade chime.

sentences.zh: 搏拊二，一在北，一在北，東西相向。

translations.literal: Two clappers, one in the north and one in the north, face each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Two clappers are set in the north, one on each side, facing each other east and west.

sentences.zh: 歌工次之，余工各位於縣後。

translations.literal: The singers are next; the remaining artisans each take their places behind the frames.
translations.idiomatic: The singers are placed next, and the remaining artisans take their stations behind the frames.

sentences.zh: 其匏竹者立於階間，重行北向，相對為首。

translations.literal: Those with gourd and bamboo instruments stand between the steps in double ranks facing north, opposite each other at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Players of gourd and bamboo instruments stand between the steps in double ranks facing north, opposite each other at the head of each rank.

sentences.zh: 享前一日，太廟令率其屬掃除廟庭之內外；

translations.literal: On the day before the offering, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple leads his subordinates to sweep the inside and outside of the temple courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the sacrifice, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple leads his subordinates to sweep the temple courtyard inside and out;

sentences.zh: 樞密院軍官一員，率軍人鏟除草穢，平治道路。

translations.literal: A military officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs leads soldiers to cut grass and weeds and level the roads.
translations.idiomatic: A military officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs leads soldiers to cut grass and weeds and level the roads.

sentences.zh: 又設七祀燎柴於廟門之外。

translations.literal: Bundles for the seven sacrifices are also set outside the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bundles for burning at the seven sacrifices are also set outside the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 又於室內鋪設神位於北牖下，當戶南向。

translations.literal: Within each chamber the spirit seat is spread below the northern window, facing south at the center of the door.
translations.idiomatic: Within each chamber the spirit seat is laid out below the northern window, facing south at the center of the doorway.

sentences.zh: 每位設黼扆一，紫綾厚褥一，薄褥一，莞席一，繅席二，虎皮次席二。

translations.literal: For each seat one embroidered screen, one thick purple silk cushion, one thin cushion, one cattail mat, two silk mats, and two tiger-skin secondary mats are set.
translations.idiomatic: For each seat there is one embroidered screen, one thick purple silk cushion, one thin cushion, one cattail mat, two silk mats, and two tiger-skin secondary mats.

sentences.zh: 時暄則用桃枝竹席，幾在筵上。

translations.literal: In warm weather peach-branch bamboo mats are used; the table is on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: In warm weather peach-branch bamboo mats are used, with the table set upon the mat.

sentences.zh: 又設三獻官拜跪褥位二，一在室內，一在室外。

translations.literal: Two bowing and kneeling mat places for the three offering officers are also set, one inside the chamber and one outside.
translations.idiomatic: Two mat stations for bowing and kneeling by the three offering officers are also set, one inside the chamber and one outside.

sentences.zh: 學士院定撰祝冊訖，書祝官於饌幕具公服書祝訖，請初獻官署御名訖，以授太廟令。

translations.literal: When the Academy of Scholarly Worthies has completed drafting the prayer text, the prayer-writing officer in official dress writes it in the food-preparation tent; when this is complete the chief offering officer is asked to affix the imperial name; it is then handed to the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Academy of Scholarly Worthies has completed drafting the prayer text, the prayer-writing officer, in official dress, writes it in the food-preparation tent. When this is done, the chief offering officer is asked to affix the imperial name, and the text is handed to the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 又設祝案於室戶外之右。

translations.literal: A prayer table is also set to the right outside the chamber door.
translations.idiomatic: A prayer table is also set to the right outside the chamber door.

sentences.zh: 又設三獻官位於殿下橫街之南，稍西，東向；

translations.literal: The place for the three offering officers is also set south of the cross street below the hall, slightly west, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: The station for the three offering officers is also set south of the cross street below the hall, slightly to the west, facing east;

sentences.zh: 亞獻終獻位稍卻，助奠七祀獻官又於其南；

translations.literal: The places for the secondary and final offering officers are set slightly back; the seven subsidiary offering officers for the seven sacrifices are set still further south;
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the secondary and final offering officers are set slightly to the rear, and the seven subsidiary offering officers for the seven sacrifices still further south;

sentences.zh: 書祝官、讀祝官、舉祝官、太廟令、太官令、良醞令、廩犧令、太廟丞、太官丞位，又於其南；

translations.literal: The places for the prayer-writing officer, prayer-reading officer, prayer-board officer, Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of Imperial Kitchens, Director of Fine Brew, Director of Sacrificial Livestock, Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Vice Director of Imperial Kitchens are set still further south;
translations.idiomatic: Still further south are the stations for the prayer-writing officer, prayer-reading officer, prayer-board officer, Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Director of the Imperial Kitchens, Director of Fine Brew, Director of Sacrificial Livestock, Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Vice Director of the Imperial Kitchens;

sentences.zh: 司尊彜、奉瓚官、奉爵官、盥洗巾篚、爵洗巾篚、蒙古太祝、蒙古巫祝、太祝、宮闈令及七祀司尊彜、盥洗巾篚，以次而南。

translations.literal: The wine-vessel steward, libation-cup-presenting officer, cup-presenting officer, hand-washing towel and basket, libation-cup-washing towel and basket, Mongol Chief Sacrificer, Mongol shaman sacrificer, Chief Sacrificer, Director of Palace Inner Quarters, and the seven-sacrifice wine-vessel stewards and hand-washing towel and basket are set in order still further south.
translations.idiomatic: In order still further south are the wine-vessel steward, libation-cup-presenting officer, cup-presenting officer, hand-washing towel and basket, libation-cup-washing towel and basket, Mongol Chief Sacrificer, Mongol shaman sacrificer, Chief Sacrificer, Director of Palace Inner Quarters, and the seven-sacrifice wine-vessel stewards with their hand-washing towel and basket.

sentences.zh: 又設齋郎位於其後。

translations.literal: The places for the fasting officers are also set behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the fasting officers are also placed behind them.

sentences.zh: 每等異位，重行，東向，北上。

translations.literal: Each rank in a separate place, in double ranks, facing east, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Each rank occupies a separate station in double ranks, facing east, with the northern position superior.

sentences.zh: 又設大禮使位於南神門東偏門稍北，北向。

translations.literal: The place for the Grand Master of Rites is also set slightly north of the eastern side gate of the southern spirit gate, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Grand Master of Rites is also set slightly north of the eastern side gate of the southern spirit gate, facing north.

sentences.zh: 又設司徒、太常卿等位於橫街之南，稍東，西向，與亞終獻相對，司徒位在北，太常卿稍卻；

translations.literal: The places for the Minister of Education, Minister of Imperial Rites, and others are also set south of the cross street, slightly east, facing west, opposite the secondary and final offering officers; the Minister of Education's place is in the north, the Minister of Imperial Rites slightly back;
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the Minister of Education, Minister of Imperial Rites, and others are also set south of the cross street, slightly to the east, facing west, opposite the secondary and final offering officers. The Minister of Education's station is to the north, the Minister of Imperial Rites' slightly to the rear;

sentences.zh: 太常同知、光祿卿、僉院、同僉院判、光祿丞、拱衛使，以次而南。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Court Commissioner, Associate Court Commissioner, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, and Commander of the Imperial Guard proceed in order to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Court Commissioner, Associate Court Commissioner, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, and Commander of the Imperial Guard are placed in order further south.

sentences.zh: 又設監祭御史位二、監禮博士位二於橫街之北，西向，以北為上。

translations.literal: Two places for the Supervising Sacrifice Censor and two for the Supervising Ritual Erudite are also set north of the cross street, facing west, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Two stations for the Supervising Sacrifice Censor and two for the Supervising Ritual Erudite are also set north of the cross street, facing west, with the northern position superior.

sentences.zh: 又設協律郎位在宮縣樂虡西北，東向，大樂丞在樂虡之間。

translations.literal: The place for the Pitch Master is also set northwest of the palace ensemble frame, facing east; the Vice Director of Imperial Music is between the frames.
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Pitch Master is also set northwest of the palace ensemble frame, facing east, with the Vice Director of Imperial Music between the frames.

sentences.zh: 又設大樂令、協律郎位於登歌樂虡之間。

translations.literal: The places for the Director of Imperial Music and Pitch Master are also set between the ascent music frames.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the Director of Imperial Music and Pitch Master are also set between the ascent music frames.

sentences.zh: 又設牲榜於東神門外，南向。

translations.literal: A sacrificial victim placard is also set outside the eastern spirit gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A sacrificial victim placard is also set outside the eastern spirit gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 設太常卿位於牲位，南向。

translations.literal: The place for the Minister of Imperial Rites is set at the victim place, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Minister of Imperial Rites is set at the victim place, facing south.

sentences.zh: 監祭御史位在太常卿之左，太官令次之，光祿丞、太官丞又次之，廩犧令位在牲西南，廩犧丞稍卻，俱北向，以右為上。

translations.literal: The place for the Supervising Sacrifice Censor is to the left of the Minister of Imperial Rites; the Director of Imperial Kitchens is next; the Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies and Vice Director of Imperial Kitchens follow; the place for the Director of Sacrificial Livestock is southwest of the victim, the Vice Director slightly back—all facing north, with right as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervising Sacrifice Censor stands to the left of the Minister of Imperial Rites, the Director of the Imperial Kitchens next, then the Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies and Vice Director of the Imperial Kitchens. The Director of Sacrificial Livestock stands southwest of the victim and the Vice Director slightly to the rear—all facing north, with the right-hand position superior.

sentences.zh: 又設諸太祝位於牲東，西向，以北為上。

translations.literal: The places for the various Chief Sacrificers are also set east of the victim, facing west, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: The stations for the various Chief Sacrificers are also set east of the victim, facing west, with the northern position superior.

sentences.zh: 又設蒙古巫祝位於牲東南，北向。

translations.literal: The place for the Mongol shaman sacrificer is also set southeast of the victim, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The station for the Mongol shaman sacrificer is also set southeast of the victim, facing north.

sentences.zh: 又設省饌位於省饌殿前，太常卿、光祿卿、光祿丞、太官令位於東，西向；

translations.literal: The place for inspecting the food offerings is also set before the food-inspection hall; the Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, and Director of Imperial Kitchens are set on the east, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The station for inspecting the food offerings is also set before the food-inspection hall. The Minister of Imperial Rites, Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, Vice Minister of Imperial Household Supplies, and Director of the Imperial Kitchens stand on the east, facing west;

sentences.zh: 監祭、監禮位於西，東向；

translations.literal: The Supervising Sacrifice and Supervising Ritual places are on the west, facing east;
